Remote control, keyboard, mouse and game controller
TVBox Remote controls Android TV and Google TV boxes. It connects over Wi-Fi or Bluetooth.
Open the menu and tap Devices. Boxes on your Wi-Fi network show automatically. Tap a box to connect.
After the first connection, the app connects to the same box again when you open it.
The phone and the box must use the same Wi-Fi network.
When you connect to a box for the first time, the TV shows a 6-character code. Type the code on the phone and tap Pair.
If the box does not show in the list, tap \"Add by IP address\". You can find the IP address on the box in Settings, then Network & Internet.
To remove a box, tap the delete icon next to it, or hold its row.
With Bluetooth, the phone acts as a Bluetooth keyboard, mouse, game controller and remote. The box needs no app and no Wi-Fi.
To pair: open Devices and tap \"Make phone visible\". On the box, open Settings, then Remotes & Accessories, then Add accessory. Select this phone and confirm the code on both screens.
After pairing, the box shows in the Bluetooth list. Tap it to connect.
Over Bluetooth, the keyboard can type only the characters of a US keyboard. Some keys, for example Input and All apps, are not available. The Settings key works on some boxes only.
Tap the mouse button on the remote. Point the phone at the TV and move it. The cursor follows. Tap the pad or the Click button to click. Drag with two fingers to scroll.
You can turn the gyro off. Then drag one finger on the pad to move the cursor, like on a laptop.
Over Bluetooth, the mouse works with no extra app.
Over Wi-Fi, install the TVBox Remote Receiver app on the box and turn on its accessibility service. The first time, the TV shows a 4-digit code. Type it on the phone.
Tap the gamepad button on the remote. The phone turns to landscape and shows a game controller with two sticks, a D-pad, A, B, X, Y, Start, Select and the shoulder buttons.
Over Bluetooth, the box sees a real game controller with analog sticks. If the controller does not work after an update, remove the phone from the Bluetooth list of the box and pair again.
Over Wi-Fi, the buttons work, the left stick works as a D-pad, and the right stick moves the mouse cursor if the receiver app is installed.
To move or resize the buttons, open Preferences, then Controller layout.
Add the TVBox Remote widget to your home screen for a small remote with a D-pad, Power, Back and Home.
If you use more than one TV box, swipe up or down on the widget to change the box. On Android 11 and earlier, tap the box name.
Select a text field on the TV, for example a search field. Then tap the keyboard button on the remote and type.
Over Wi-Fi, the text on the TV changes while you type. The Send key of the phone keyboard sends Enter.
Over Wi-Fi, the phone keyboard can open by itself when the box shows its keyboard.
No box in the list: make sure that the phone and the box use the same network. Some guest networks and mesh networks block device discovery. Use \"Add by IP address\".
The connection fails after pairing: forget the box in Devices and pair again.
\"The box has a new certificate\": the box was reset, or another device uses its address. Forget the box and pair again.
The mouse does not work over Wi-Fi: make sure that the receiver app is installed and that its accessibility service is on.
Bluetooth does not connect: remove the phone from the Bluetooth list of the box, remove the box from the phone, and pair again.
A simple remote control for Android TV and Google TV boxes, with a keyboard, a gyro mouse and a game controller.

Wi-Fi: the Android TV Remote protocol (version 2), the same one as the Google TV remote. Bluetooth: the phone acts as a Bluetooth HID keyboard, mouse, game controller and remote. Mouse over Wi-Fi: the TVBox Remote Receiver app on the box.
The app talks only to devices on your local network. It collects no data.
The description of the Android TV Remote protocol comes from the open-source androidtvremote2 project.
Right stick, not available: the receiver app is not connected
Over Wi-Fi, the left stick works as a D-pad.
Over Wi-Fi, the left stick works as a D-pad. The right stick needs the receiver app.
Drag a control to move it. Tap a control to change its size.
A small remote: D-pad, Power, Back and Home in two rows.
A small remote with a D-pad, Power, Back and Home.
Add a TV box in the app
Tap here to find the TV boxes on your Wi-Fi.
Tap the box that you want to control. The TV then shows a code. You type it on the phone.
Make sure that the box is on and on the same Wi-Fi as the phone. Or tap Add by IP address. The box shows its address in Settings, Network & Internet.
%1$s is connected. Use the buttons to control the TV. To see this tour again, open Help in the menu.
Choose how the phone works as a mouse
Bluetooth needs no app on the box. The receiver works over Wi-Fi.
Tap here. Then on the box, open Settings, Remotes & Accessories, Add accessory, and select this phone.
The phone can move a cursor on the TV. Pick one way. You do this only once.
No app on the box. The phone becomes a Bluetooth mouse.
Mouse over Wi-Fi. A one-time install on the box.
Open Google Play on the TV
On the TV, go to Apps and open Google Play Store. You can use the D-pad on this phone.
Search for Downloader. Select Downloader by AFTVnews, then Install. It is free.
Open Downloader. Select the address field, type this address, then select Go.
Waiting for the box. The next step opens when the download ends.
Select Install. If the TV says that it cannot install unknown apps, select Settings, allow Downloader, go back, and select Install again.

TV says “App blocked to protect your device”? Select Got it. On the TV, open the Play Store, then your profile, Play Protect and Settings. Turn off Scan apps with Play Protect. Install the receiver again, then turn the scan back on.
Open TVBox Remote Receiver. Select Open accessibility settings, then TVBox Remote mouse, and turn it on.
Switch is gray? Open Settings, Apps, TVBox Remote Receiver. In its menu, select Allow restricted settings.
